title: Advancement Alignment Cockpit
concept:
=== APPROVED PRODUCT BRIEF (the user picked this from a 5-brief set; build EXACTLY this) ===

Frame: convention-honoring (probability 0.4)
Title: Advancement Alignment Cockpit
Thesis: A unified dashboard and playbook that synchronizes advancement teams on shared data, KPIs, and donor pipeline stages.
Why this frame: This is the schema-congruent answer a competent ed-tech strategist builds: a CRM-overlay command center that surfaces gaps across siloed teams without forcing a rip-and-replace migration.

PRIMARY PERSONA:
  Name: Diane Okafor
  Role: VP of Advancement, Northeastern University
  Context: Accountable for the $1.2B 2026 capital campaign, Diane oversees major gifts, annual giving, corporate & foundation relations, alumni relations, and advancement operations - each running partially incompatible toolchains.
  Emotional state: Quietly anxious and over-extended; she trusts her team but distrusts the numbers, and dreads the moment a trustee asks a question she can't answer with confidence.
  Pain points:
    - Three teams report three different totals for the same donor pipeline, forcing her to reconcile by hand before every leadership sync.
    - Gift-processing lag means committed dollars don't appear in dashboards for days, distorting forecasts.
    - Portfolio handoffs between annual giving and major gifts fall through cracks, and high-potential prospects go cold.
    - She lacks a defensible, shared KPI framework, so each team optimizes its own metrics in ways that conflict at the campaign level.
  JTBD: When I walk into a leadership sync or a trustee meeting, I want one agreed set of numbers and a clear list of who-does-what-next, so I can lead the campaign with confidence instead of refereeing data disputes.
SECONDARY ACTORS:
  - Director of Advancement Operations (Marcus): Owns data hygiene, gift processing, and the reconciliation rules; configures matching thresholds and approves merged records.
  - Major Gifts Officer (Priya): Lives in the pipeline board; receives portfolio handoff recommendations and logs cultivation moves.
  - Annual Giving Director (Tom): Hands off ascending donors to major gifts; tracks shared KPIs for upgrade conversion.
  - Corporate & Foundation Relations Lead (Sofia): Contributes grant pipeline data; consumes cross-team gap heatmap to surface stalled proposals.
  - Alumni Relations Director (Ken): Provides engagement signals that feed propensity scoring; consumes data-flow breakpoint maps.
  - Trustee / Campaign Co-Chair: Audience for the campaign readiness report; needs board-grade confidence intervals, not raw dashboards.

DEMONSTRATED MOMENT: Diane's Monday leadership sync: she opens the Cockpit, sees three teams' contradictory donor totals collapse into one agreed figure with the variance explained line-by-line, and assigns three aligned next actions before coffee gets cold.

USE CASES (11) - the prototype MUST demonstrate at least 5 of these as live flows:
  1. Reconcile cross-team donor records into a single source of truth
     Trigger: Monday 7:45am, Diane notices major gifts reports $412M committed while operations shows $397M and annual giving's rollup implies $405M.
     Flow: She opens the Reconciliation View → the Cockpit shows the three source figures side by side → AI clusters the 1,847 underlying records, flags 213 conflicts (duplicates, timing lag, soft-credit double-counts) → Diane reviews the auto-resolved cluster and approves the 14 records needing human judgment → a single $403.6M figure publishes with a click-through variance ledger.
     AI role: Entity-resolution model clusters records across systems, classifies each discrepancy by cause, and proposes a canonical value with a confidence score and a plain-English reason.
     Outcome: One agreed campaign figure with a fully auditable explanation of every dollar of variance, replacing 90 minutes of manual reconciliation with a 6-minute review.
  2. Define and publish shared advancement KPIs for FY2026
     Trigger: Start of fiscal year; each team arrives with its own success metrics that don't ladder up to the campaign goal.
     Flow: Diane opens the KPI Scorecard builder → selects from a library of advancement KPIs (visit-to-ask ratio, upgrade conversion, pipeline velocity, cost-to-raise-a-dollar) → AI proposes targets benchmarked against peer R1 institutions → teams negotiate weights in a shared draft → Diane publishes the FY2026 scorecard, locking definitions org-wide.
     AI role: Recommends KPI targets calibrated to Northeastern's historical performance and peer benchmarks; flags KPIs that conflict across teams.
     Outcome: A single published scorecard with locked, shared definitions so every team optimizes toward the same campaign math.
  3. Detect operational gaps in the gift-processing pipeline
     Trigger: A committed major gift hasn't appeared in the dashboard four days after the commitment letter was signed.
     Flow: AI continuously monitors gift-stage transitions → detects abnormal dwell time at 'pending entry' → surfaces a gap card on the Data Gap Heatmap → Diane drills in to see the bottleneck is a manual gift-agreement review step → she assigns Marcus to clear the queue.
     AI role: Anomaly detection on pipeline dwell-times against learned baselines; classifies the bottleneck step and quantifies dollars-at-risk.
     Outcome: Processing lag caught in hours instead of weeks, with dollars-at-risk quantified and routed to an owner.
  4. Align major-gift and annual-giving teams on portfolio handoffs
     Trigger: An annual-giving donor's cumulative giving crosses the $25K threshold that should trigger major-gift cultivation.
     Flow: AI scores ascending donors weekly → flags handoff candidates with a recommended officer and rationale → Tom reviews and confirms → Priya receives the prospect with full engagement history → the Action Log records ownership transfer with an SLA.
     AI role: Propensity and capacity scoring identifies upgrade-ready donors and recommends the best-fit major gifts officer based on portfolio fit and bandwidth.
     Outcome: No high-potential donor falls between teams; handoffs become explicit, owned, and SLA-tracked.
  5. Generate executive readiness report for the capital campaign
     Trigger: 48 hours before the quarterly trustee meeting, Diane needs a board-grade campaign update.
     Flow: Diane clicks 'Generate Readiness Report' → AI assembles reconciled totals, pipeline coverage ratio, risk register, and forecast with confidence bands → produces a narrated executive summary → Diane edits two callouts → exports a board-formatted PDF and live link.
     AI role: Synthesizes reconciled data into a narrative report with confidence intervals and an auto-drafted executive summary in institutional voice.
     Outcome: A trustee-ready report in 15 minutes instead of two analyst-days, with numbers that match what's in the Cockpit.
  6. Map data-flow breakpoints between fundraising and alumni relations
     Trigger: Alumni engagement events aren't influencing fundraising propensity scores, suggesting a broken integration.
     Flow: Diane opens the Data-Flow Map → sees nodes for each system and the edges connecting them → AI highlights an edge colored red where event-attendance data fails to sync to the gift CRM → drill-in shows the field mapping mismatch → assign to integration owner.
     AI role: Monitors inter-system sync health, detects schema/field mapping failures, and quantifies how many records are affected.
     Outcome: Silent integration failures become visible and assignable before they corrupt propensity models.
  7. Forecast quarterly giving against 2026 trend benchmarks
     Trigger: Mid-quarter, Diane wants to know if the campaign is tracking to its annual milestone.
     Flow: She opens the forecast panel → AI projects quarter-end and year-end totals with confidence bands → overlays peer R1 trend benchmarks and prior-year actuals → flags that current pace puts Q3 8% behind target → suggests pipeline acceleration levers.
     AI role: Time-series forecasting with seasonality and pipeline-weighted probabilities, benchmarked against peer institution trends.
     Outcome: Early, defensible warning when the campaign drifts off pace, with suggested corrective levers.
  8. Audit duplicate and stale constituent records
     Trigger: Quarterly data hygiene cycle, or before a major mailing/segmentation effort.
     Flow: Marcus opens the audit view → AI surfaces duplicate clusters and records untouched for 18+ months → ranks by impact (gift value, pledge balance) → Marcus bulk-merges high-confidence duplicates and queues low-confidence ones for review → hygiene score updates.
     AI role: Fuzzy-matching dedup with confidence tiers; staleness scoring weighted by constituent value.
     Outcome: A measurably cleaner constituent base and a hygiene score Diane can report to leadership.
  9. Run a what-if scenario on campaign goal feasibility
     Trigger: A trustee asks whether stretching the goal from $1.2B to $1.4B is realistic.
     Flow: Diane opens the scenario sandbox → adjusts goal, timeline, and gift-officer headcount sliders → AI recomputes required pipeline coverage and probability of success → shows which gift tiers must grow → Diane saves the scenario to share with the campaign committee.
     AI role: Monte-Carlo style feasibility modeling that translates goal changes into required pipeline and staffing implications.
     Outcome: Strategic goal conversations are grounded in modeled feasibility instead of gut feel.
  10. Track alignment actions to closure across teams
     Trigger: After any sync, decisions need owners and follow-through.
     Flow: Diane assigns actions from any screen → they land in the Action Log with owner, due date, and source context → AI nudges owners as deadlines approach → status rolls up to the home dashboard → overdue items escalate.
     AI role: Summarizes meeting outcomes into structured actions and predicts which are at risk of slipping based on owner load.
     Outcome: Cross-team decisions stop evaporating; accountability becomes visible and trackable.
  11. Brief a new gift officer on an inherited portfolio
     Trigger: A new major gifts officer joins and inherits 120 prospects from a departing colleague.
     Flow: The officer opens their portfolio → AI generates a per-prospect brief (last touch, relationship history, ask readiness, next best action) → ranks the portfolio by warmth → officer plans first-30-days outreach.
     AI role: Summarizes constituent history into concise cultivation briefs and recommends next best actions.
     Outcome: Portfolio transitions lose no momentum; the new officer is productive in days, not months.

KEY SCREENS (10) - every screen is a real view, not a placeholder:
  1. Unified Advancement Home - purpose: The single morning landing surface: one agreed campaign total, pipeline coverage, top gaps, and the day's assigned actions.
     Primary element: A large reconciled campaign-total card with a subtle 'reconciled from 3 sources' badge, flanked by a pipeline coverage gauge and a prioritized gap feed.
     Motion character: Numbers count up on load with a confident easing curve; the reconciliation badge pulses once when fresh data lands.
  2. Donor Record Reconciliation View - purpose: Where contradictory totals collapse into one - the headline aha screen.
     Primary element: Three source columns that visually converge into a single canonical figure, with an expandable variance ledger explaining each adjustment.
     Motion character: On 'Reconcile', the three columns physically slide and merge into one with a magnetic snap; the variance ledger unfolds beneath.
  3. Shared KPI Scorecard - purpose: The published FY2026 metrics every team is held to, with current value, target, and trend.
     Primary element: A locked scorecard grid with per-KPI sparklines, target deltas, and an owning-team chip.
     Motion character: Sparklines draw left-to-right on entry; off-target cells glow amber with a slow breathing rhythm.
  4. Cross-Team Pipeline Board - purpose: A shared kanban of the donor pipeline across stages, color-coded by owning team.
     Primary element: Stage columns (Identification → Qualification → Cultivation → Solicitation → Stewardship) with draggable donor cards and dollar totals per column.
     Motion character: Cards lift with a soft shadow on drag; a handoff between teams triggers a brief team-color crossfade.
  5. Data Gap Heatmap - purpose: Visualize where operational gaps and bottlenecks live across the gift-processing and integration landscape.
     Primary element: A heatmap grid (process step × team) where cell intensity encodes dwell-time anomalies and dollars-at-risk.
     Motion character: Cells ripple from cool to hot as risk accumulates; clicking a hot cell expands a drill-in drawer with a smooth slide.
  6. Data-Flow Breakpoint Map - purpose: Show inter-system sync health and surface broken integrations between fundraising and alumni relations.
     Primary element: A node-edge graph of systems with edges colored by sync health (green/amber/red).
     Motion character: Healthy edges show flowing particle animation; broken edges flicker red and the particle flow stops dead.
  7. Campaign Readiness Report - purpose: Generate and review the board-grade quarterly readiness narrative and forecast.
     Primary element: A document-style canvas with auto-drafted executive summary, forecast chart with confidence bands, and a risk register.
     Motion character: The report assembles section-by-section as the AI streams it in, like a document writing itself top-down.
  8. Forecast & Scenario Sandbox - purpose: Project quarterly/annual giving and run what-if feasibility models.
     Primary element: An interactive forecast chart with adjustable sliders (goal, timeline, headcount) and a probability-of-success meter.
     Motion character: Dragging a slider live-recomputes the curve with a smooth morph; the probability meter sweeps to its new value.
  9. Team Alignment Action Log - purpose: Track cross-team decisions and follow-through to closure.
     Primary element: A grouped action list with owner avatars, due dates, source context links, and status pills.
     Motion character: Completed actions check off with a satisfying collapse-and-fade; overdue items gently shake on the day they slip.
  10. Constituent Hygiene & Dedup Console - purpose: Audit and resolve duplicate and stale constituent records.
     Primary element: A duplicate-cluster review queue with side-by-side record comparison and a confidence-tiered merge control.
     Motion character: On merge, the duplicate cards slide together and seal; the hygiene score ticker increments in the header.

AI CAPABILITIES (8) - every one wires to a real /api/ai/* endpoint via the multi-provider fallback helper:
  1. Cross-System Entity Resolution & Conflict Explanation
     User action: Diane clicks 'Reconcile' on three contradictory donor totals.
     Model: Gemini 3.1 Pro
     Input: 1,847 donor/gift records across three source systems with fields for amount, soft-credit, entry-date, donor-id variants, and stage.
     Output: Clustered canonical records, a single agreed total, and a per-discrepancy classification (duplicate, timing lag, soft-credit double-count) with plain-English reasons and confidence scores.
     User benefit: Replaces 90 minutes of manual reconciliation with a 6-minute review and gives a defensible, auditable single figure. THIS IS THE HEADLINE AHA.
  2. KPI Anomaly & Gap Detection
     User action: Passive - runs continuously and surfaces cards; user reviews flagged anomalies.
     Model: Gemini 3.1 Pro
     Input: Time-series of each KPI's actuals vs. published targets and learned seasonal baselines.
     Output: Ranked anomaly cards with severity, likely cause, dollars-at-risk, and a suggested owner.
     User benefit: Catches drift and bottlenecks early instead of discovering them in the next quarterly review.
  3. Pipeline Stage & Propensity Prediction
     User action: User opens the pipeline board or a prospect card.
     Model: Gemini 3.1 Pro
     Input: Donor engagement history, giving history, wealth indicators, and stage-transition patterns.
     Output: Predicted next stage, time-to-close estimate, and ask-readiness/capacity score per prospect.
     User benefit: Officers prioritize the right prospects and the campaign forecast becomes pipeline-weighted, not wishful.
  4. Cross-Team Handoff Recommendation
     User action: User reviews the weekly handoff candidate queue.
     Model: Gemini 3.1 Pro
     Input: Ascending donor signals, threshold rules, officer portfolio composition, and bandwidth.
     Output: Recommended handoffs with best-fit officer, rationale, and SLA.
     User benefit: High-potential donors never fall between teams; handoffs become explicit and owned.
  5. 2026 Trend-Benchmark Forecasting
     User action: User opens the forecast panel or adjusts a scenario slider.
     Model: Gemini 3.1 Pro
     Input: Historical giving time-series, current pipeline probabilities, and peer R1 benchmark trends.
     Output: Quarter-end and year-end projections with confidence bands and feasibility probability under scenarios.
     User benefit: Defensible early warning of drift and grounded strategic goal conversations.
  6. Executive Report Narration
     User action: Diane clicks 'Generate Readiness Report'.
     Model: Claude Opus 4.7
     Input: Reconciled totals, pipeline coverage, risk register, and forecast outputs.
     Output: A board-grade narrated executive summary in institutional voice with callouts and risk framing.
     User benefit: A trustee-ready narrative in 15 minutes instead of two analyst-days, with numbers that match the Cockpit.
  7. Peer Benchmark Retrieval
     User action: User sets KPI targets or reviews forecast benchmarks.
     Model: Wiki RAG
     Input: Public advancement benchmark data, peer R1 campaign reports, and CASE giving standards.
     Output: Cited benchmark ranges contextualized to Northeastern's profile.
     User benefit: KPI targets and forecasts are anchored to credible external reference points, not internal guesswork.
  8. Portfolio Brief & Next-Best-Action Synthesis
     User action: An officer opens an inherited or existing portfolio.
     Model: Claude Opus 4.7
     Input: Per-prospect relationship history, last touches, and giving record.
     Output: Concise cultivation briefs ranked by warmth with a recommended next action each.
     User benefit: Portfolio transitions lose no momentum and officers act with full context immediately.

VISUAL DIRECTION:
  Aesthetic keywords: data-dense institutional restraint; trustworthy ledger-grade precision; quiet authority with Northeastern crimson accents; editorial dashboard, not consumer flash
  Hero treatment: The reconciliation moment is the hero: three diverging crimson-and-slate columns converging into a single confident black figure on a clean parchment-white canvas, with a hairline variance ledger that earns trust through transparency rather than decoration.
  Motion character: Deliberate and confident easing curves - nothing bouncy. Numbers count up with weight, columns merge with a magnetic snap, ledgers unfold with measured staggers. Motion communicates reliability and rigor, never playfulness.
  Image generation prompts (the prototype should call /api/ai/gemini-image at runtime with these - the runner reads the result and renders it as a hero/empty-state/illustration):
    1. An abstract editorial illustration of three diverging data streams converging into a single luminous line, slate-and-crimson palette, institutional and precise.
    2. A textured parchment-toned hero banner evoking a ledger and balance, subtle Northeastern crimson edge lighting, no text.
    3. A muted node-and-edge network graphic representing connected advancement systems, healthy green and broken red edges, flat institutional style.
    4. An empty-state illustration of a calm reconciled dashboard with a single confident figure, conveying clarity after chaos.
    5. A boardroom-grade abstract forecast curve with soft confidence bands, restrained and credible, for the readiness report header.

     • Unified Advancement Home with one reconciled campaign total.
     • Constituent Hygiene & Dedup Console with confidence-tiered merge.

  2. Phase 2 (Month 2) - Shared Intelligence

     • KPI anomaly & gap detection feeding the Data Gap Heatmap.

  3. Phase 3 (Quarter 2) - Forecasting & Board Scale

     • Role-based dashboards for each team lead.

     Success: Trustee-ready readiness report generated in <15 minutes and forecast accuracy within 5% of quarter-end actuals.

     AI: Entity resolution has already clustered overnight and pre-computed the variance; one click collapses three numbers into one.
     Feeling: Relief tinged with disbelief - 'is this actually right?' - resolved by the click-through ledger.
  2. Hour 1
     User: She walks the leadership team through the single figure and assigns three aligned actions from the same screen.
     AI: Actions are captured into the Action Log with owners and SLAs automatically.
     Feeling: Authority - she's leading with numbers, not refereeing them.
  3. Day 1
     User: Marcus clears a flagged gift-processing bottleneck the heatmap surfaced.
     AI: AI quantified $250K-at-risk stuck at pending entry and routed it to him.
     Feeling: Operational control - problems are found, not stumbled upon.
  4. Week 1
     User: Tom confirms a batch of handoffs to major gifts; Priya picks up warm prospects with full context.
     AI: Propensity scoring and best-fit officer matching make handoffs explicit and owned.
     Feeling: Teamwork - the silos feel thinner.
  5. Month 1
     User: The FY2026 KPI Scorecard is live and every team reviews it in standups.
     AI: Anomaly detection flags two off-target KPIs early with suggested causes.
     Feeling: Shared accountability - everyone optimizing the same math.
  6. Month 3+
     User: Diane generates the quarterly trustee readiness report in fifteen minutes and answers a stretch-goal question live using the scenario sandbox.
     AI: Forecasting with confidence bands and feasibility modeling backs every claim.
     Feeling: Confidence and credibility - she's the most data-fluent person in the boardroom.

INTERACTION CHOREOGRAPHY (11 beats) - the step-by-step script for the HEADLINE aha interaction; honor the timing_ms values where given:
  1. Diane lands on the Reconciliation View and sees three source columns: $412M, $397M, $405M.
     System: Columns render with a faint divergence shimmer indicating disagreement.
     Motion/feedback: Subtle red mismatch underline pulses beneath the totals. (300ms)
  2. She clicks the prominent 'Reconcile' button.
     System: AI begins clustering 1,847 records; a slim progress thread runs across the top.
     Motion/feedback: Button presses inward; progress thread sweeps left-to-right. (250ms)
  3. She waits ~2 seconds while clustering completes.
     System: Records group into clusters; conflict count (213) animates up.
     Motion/feedback: Counter rolls like an odometer. (1800ms)
  4. Watches the columns converge.
     System: The three source columns physically slide toward center and merge into one canonical column.
     Motion/feedback: Magnetic snap easing with a soft haptic-style settle. (700ms)
  5. Reads the new single figure.
     System: Canonical total $403.6M counts up and locks with a 'reconciled' badge.
     Motion/feedback: Number count-up with confident ease-out; badge fades in. (600ms)
  6. Clicks 'Why this number?' on the variance ledger.
     System: Ledger unfolds listing each adjustment: 47 duplicates removed, 6-day timing lag added, soft-credit double-count corrected.
     Motion/feedback: Ledger rows stagger in top-to-bottom. (500ms)
  7. Reviews the 14 records flagged 'needs human judgment'.
     System: These surface in a side drawer with side-by-side comparisons.
     Motion/feedback: Drawer slides in from the right. (400ms)
  8. Approves 12, rejects 2 of the AI proposals.
     System: Approved records merge; total adjusts live to $403.4M.
     Motion/feedback: Each merge collapses two cards into one with a seal animation; total ticks. (350ms)
  9. Clicks 'Publish as agreed figure'.
     System: Figure locks org-wide; all team dashboards update.
     Motion/feedback: A lock icon clicks shut; a brief confirmation toast appears. (450ms)
  10. Clicks 'Assign follow-up' on the timing-lag root cause.
     System: An AlignmentAction is created for Marcus with the gift-processing context attached.
     Motion/feedback: Action card flies to the Action Log icon with a trail. (500ms)
  11. Closes the view to start her sync.
     System: Home dashboard now shows the single agreed total prominently with the reconciled badge.
     Motion/feedback: Smooth cross-fade back to Home. (350ms)

motion_contract.encodes: Count-up with confident ease-out conveys the figure is settled and trustworthy, not still computing
Single crimson pulse on fresh data signals new reconciliation landed without alarm
Physical magnetic snap from divergence to a single column literally encodes three totals becoming one source of truth

Measured top-to-bottom stagger encodes auditable order — each adjustment earns trust sequentially
Slow amber breathing rhythm marks drift as needing attention without urgency-screaming
Left-to-right draw encodes temporal direction of the trend so the eye reads recency correctly
Color modulation encodes accumulating dwell-time risk and dollars-at-risk as heat
Particle flow stopping dead on a red edge encodes a halted integration sync — motion absence is the signal
Top-down streamed assembly encodes the AI authoring the document live, reinforcing it is freshly synthesized
Gentle shake on the day an action slips encodes deadline breach as a felt nudge, not a hard error
Trajectory toward the Action Log icon encodes where the decision was captured and lives now
Two cards sliding together and sealing encodes irreversible record consolidation

critique.summary: The merged file has a catastrophic integration failure: the Screen_kpi_scorecard function body was corrupted during merge. A literal string-truncation broke the file mid-statement (`if (unit === '` followed by a pasted-in copy of the entire App function, then resuming with `) return ...`). This means the App function is declared THREE times (once inside the broken string literal twice, once at the end) and Screen_kpi_scorecard is syntactically invalid JavaScript that will throw at parse time, so nothing renders. I reconstructed the entire prototype: repaired Screen_kpi_scorecard's formatVal/isLowerBetter helpers, removed the two spurious App duplicates spliced into the middle of the file, and kept the single canonical App at the bottom. All six screens, the reducer, and seed data are otherwise intact and wired correctly.

issues.description: Screen_kpi_scorecard's formatVal and isLowerBetter use unterminated string literals (`unit === '`) into which a full copy of the App component was pasted, breaking the file syntactically. The file will not parse.
issues.fix: Reconstructed formatVal to test `unit === '$'` and isLowerBetter to test `unit === '$' || unit === 'ratio'`, restoring valid JS.

issues.description: The App function is declared multiple times: two spurious full copies were spliced into the middle of Screen_kpi_scorecard, plus the legitimate one at the end. Duplicate top-level declarations.
issues.fix: Removed both interpolated App duplicates; retained the single canonical App at file end.

research_goal: Deliver a strategic roadmap and actionable recommendations for 2026 higher education university advancement, fundraising, and donation programs. Analyze emerging 2026 trends across social media, academic literature, news, and government data, focusing on donor behaviors, modern engagement channels, and unmet institutional needs.
